Subject: Production: sudden 5xx spike and throughput collapse in us-west-1

Hannah —

We are seeing a sharp rise in 5xx responses starting ~07:55 PDT and throughput for our traffic routed to us-west-1 dropped by ~60%. Latency is up ~300ms on average and some customers are reporting timeouts. Our internal monitoring shows a sustained increase in model decode errors and a backlog on the gateway layer.

Attached are a short support dump and the ticket we opened (8872). Can you confirm whether Redwood can route our traffic away from us-west-1 while you investigate? We need a mitigation plan and an ETA.

Anya

Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden 5xx spike and throughput collapse in us-west-1

Looping in SRE and account lead. Customer impact: Larkspur production (critical). Key asks from customer: immediate traffic steering out of AZ1 (us-west-1) to reduce error surface, and an ETA for root cause.

Quick facts:
- 5xx spike started ~07:55 PDT, sustained for +2 hours at peak
- Affects both generation and embeddings calls; error payload mentions ‘KV cache exhaustion’ in some cases
- Customer-rate: heavy ppq (prompt-per-query) workload, they are on Dedicated pool with regional preference pinned to us-west-1

Recommended immediate actions (please confirm):
1) Approve rapid geo-toggle to route Larkspur to nearby us-west-2/ us-east-2 fallback region (temporary)
2) Apply temporary request throttling (soft-limit) to flatten burst while cache pruning runs
3) Capture full runtime traces and share with customer (attach as follow-up)

Jordan — can you confirm whether we have capacity and a compatible model variant in fallback regions? Marissa / Aditya — I’ll need exec approval for cross-region priority routing and an apology/credit comms package if we escalate.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden 5xx spike and throughput collapse in us-west-1

We can execute the geo-toggle. Quick operational readout:
- Confirmed: us-west-1 AZ1 has elevated 5xx from runtime layer (kernel OOM + cache miss amplification) — correlates with customer’s logs.
- Capacity: us-west-2 has compatible model variant (quantized) with ~85% of the same throughput; us-east-2 has full parity but higher latency.
- Risk: partial degradation on output distributions when switching to quantized variant (low risk for Larkspur use-case per prior eval).

Planned steps (I will lead):
A) Trigger priority re-route policy for Larkspur to failover to us-west-2 (start +10m after approval)
B) Enable conservative throttling: cap concurrency by 20% for 30 minutes while we stabilize cache and clear KV backlog
C) Roll collection: enable full traces and incremental logs to S3 bucket (link to follow)
D) Post-mortem window: schedule 1-hour bridge at 10:30 PDT; invite customer and SRE leads

If we get exec sign-off (Marissa), I will start the geo-toggle and notify customer. Prep note: expected short-term latency increase +40–80ms when switching to us-west-2 variant.

Jordan Blake

Anya —

Quick update and actions taken:
- At 11:15 PDT we initiated a priority geo-toggle to route Larkspur traffic away from us-west-1 to us-west-2.
- Jordan enabled a conservative concurrency cap (-20%) for 30 minutes to reduce cache amplification while we stabilize.
- Early telemetry: 5xx rate down from 6.2% to 0.9% within 12 minutes of the toggle; end-to-end latency increased by ~65ms on average (expected for quantized variant).
- We uploaded full traces and logs to shared S3: s3://redwood-support/larkspur/RED-8872/ (Anya: you'll get an access link shortly).
- Scheduled bridge: 10:30 PDT (we will run the post-mortem and next steps; calendar invite sent).

Customer ask/next steps for Redwood:
- Confirm whether Larkspur wants continued routing to us-west-2 until a permanent remediation is in place or a rollback back to us-west-1 after cleanup.
- We will provide a detailed RCA and remediation timeline within 48 hours; one-week credit approved by Marissa.

Apologies for the interruption — we’ll keep you updated in the bridge.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
